Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, the learned counsel representing first informant, upon consideration of material on record, evidence, gravity and nature of offence, accusations made as well as complicity of applicant coupled with the fact that in the F.I.R. giving rise to present application for bail, there is no allegation with regard to commission of rape by applicant upon the prosecutrix, the prosecution story as unfolded in the F.I.R has been supported by the prosecutrix in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text:
However, the prosecutrix has departed from her previous statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. in her subsequent statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., no explanation has been offered with regard to the embellishment made by the prosecutrix in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. as per the judgement of the Apex Court in Phool Singh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, (2022) 2 SCC 74 conviction of an accused can be maintained for an offence of rape or sexual assault even in absence of medical evidence and on the solitary statement of the prosecutrix, however, in the present case, when the statements of the prosecutrix referred to above when taken together do not fall in the category of Impeccable evidence, police report (charge-sheet) in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. has already been submitted therefore the entire evidence sought to relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallised, yet in spite of above no such circumstance could be pointed out by the learned A.G.A.
necessitating the custodial arrest of applicant during the pendency of trial, the clean antecedents of applicant, the period of incarceration undergone by applicant but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, applicant has made out a case for bail 11.

sentences.text:
The following arguments made by Shri Karunesh Mishra, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant,
which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Ramraj Pandey, learned counsel assisted by Shri Subham Pandey, learned counsel for the first informant and Shri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victims were wrongly shown as minor of 17 and 14 years respectively in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.
2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victims were incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victims' parents to give them an advantage in life.

sentences.text: There is no lawful basis for the age related entry of the victims in the school records.
sentences._hearing_file: Naushad vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 September, 2024.json

sentences.text: The school records disclosing their age as 17 and 14 years respectively are unreliable.
sentences._hearing_file: Naushad vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 September, 2024.json
